seo_title: Anti-Scam Case Study: Scam Content by Industry | SOMIN
description: SOMIN read 13,324 posts and ads from 34 brands in 9 industries: government bodies gave 51% of their content to scams, banks 10%, most others near 0%.
eyebrow: Brand case study · Scam awareness · Singapore
h1: Government gives 51% of its content to scams, most brands almost none
lede: SOMIN's custom study read 13,324 posts and ads from 34 Singapore brands in 9 industries. Government and anti-scam bodies gave 51% of their content to scams, banks 10% and most others 0%.
meta_line: A SOMIN custom study · 5 Dec 2023 to 5 Dec 2024 · Singapore

challenge.title: Which brands talk about scams, how often and to whom
challenge.body: Scams take many forms, so the study asked which brands discuss them, how much, and which scam types and audiences they cover.

approach.title: 13,324 posts and ads from 34 brands, read for scams
points: Checked the 34 brands' websites for scam messaging.
Collected 13,324 Instagram, Facebook and Ads Library items.
Measured each industry's scam share and classified scam types and targets.
Mapped vulnerable moments for lonely people exposed to love scams.

findings_title: Government at 51%, banks at 10%, most others at 0%

findings.title: Government bodies give 51% of content to scams
findings.body: 574 of 1,118 items from government and anti-scam institutions. Banks came second at 10%, 602 of 6,230.

findings.title: Six industries sit at 0% scam content
findings.body: E-commerce, education, employment, insurance, NGO and travel brands; logistics sat at 3%.

findings.title: Banks lead on financial scams, with 247 items
findings.body: Phishing followed at 82. Government bodies focused most on general scam behaviour (195).

delivered.title: A scam content map, 20 scam types and 6 vulnerable moments
points: Top 20 scam types and targets for banks and government bodies
6 love-scam vulnerable moments with triggers and inner voices
A sample character and story of a late-night love scam

quote.text: In lonely silence, our longing for love can blind us to hidden lies.

outcome.title: Scam warnings sit with two sectors, so target vulnerable moments
outcome.body: Two sectors carry most scam messaging, across many types, which may reinforce some kinds of awareness while drowning out others. Vulnerable moments are sharper: one audience, one scam type, one moment.

faq.q: Which industries did the study cover?
faq.a: Banking, e-commerce and retail, education, employment and recruitment, government and anti-scam institutions, insurance, logistics, NGOs and travel.

faq.q: Why do so few brands talk about scams?
faq.a: Brands may see scams as a communication crisis, not a public service message, and warnings could undercut consumer trust.
Moments when an audience is most exposed. For love scams the study maps 6, such as late-night isolation, post-breakup sadness and Valentine's Day.
